display.purpose: The 'Gambit' wordmark in the header (23px). Single largest label in the UI; nothing competes.

headline.purpose: Panel titles ('Script', 'Setup'). Uppercase, compact; a label, not a heading.

title.purpose: Tab labels and chrome button text. Compact uppercase variant (10.5-11px/700) carries section labels, the view toggle, and upload buttons.

numeric.purpose: Time-readout (mm:ss.t / mm:ss.t). Mono so digit width is stable across frames; the readout never reflows during playback.

body.purpose: Script editor textarea and the move list's mainline moves. Mono, 1.7 line-height because users read and write here.

caption.purpose: The working-surface small tier (11.5px mono): panel hints, footer, FEN input, variation flows, speed segments, inline error rows.

label.purpose: The micro-metadata floor (10.5px mono): time-tick labels, time chips, filenames, the move-number rail. The system's smallest type; anything smaller aliases on downscaled recordings.

subtitle.purpose: The subtitle strip only. CJK-first stack, 21px/600 (19px on mobile), sized to survive a 480p downscale.

shadows.name: board-ambient
shadows.purpose: The studio floor under the board. Use only on the board; the only structural shadow.

shadows.name: brand-bloom
shadows.purpose: Colored bloom under the single primary-action button (Play). Reserved; do not duplicate across adjacent buttons.

shadows.name: logo-bloom
shadows.purpose: Brand bloom plus ground shadow under the header wordmark tile. One instance; never extended to other header elements.

shadows.name: scrub-thumb-halo
shadows.purpose: Playhead halo on the timeline scrubber. Use only on the scrub thumb.

shadows.name: playhead-strand
shadows.purpose: The vertical strand crossing the timeline ruler from above the marker pins through the rail and ticks. A 1px-wide DOM element painted with a top-to-bottom alpha gradient on sodium-chalk. Reads at recording resolution; capped at the rail center by the scrub-thumb.

motion.name: ease-piece-slide
motion.purpose: Piece movement easing. Exponential ease-out tuned to land the piece on the destination square without overshoot.

motion.name: ease-state
motion.purpose: Default for chrome transitions (hover lifts, opacity fades, color shifts).

motion.name: duration-piece
motion.purpose: Piece slide duration. Functional, not decorative; do not shorten below 280ms (illegible) or above 480ms (sluggish).

motion.name: duration-transform
motion.purpose: Capture/promotion scale and opacity transitions inside the piece component.

motion.name: duration-capture-flash
motion.purpose: Three-stage capture flash on the captured square (capture-ember radial pop).

motion.name: duration-state
motion.purpose: Interactive-state transitions: tab/segment/marker hover, opacity, pin transform scale.

motion.name: duration-chrome
motion.purpose: Move-list hover transitions and other low-stakes chrome state changes.

motion.name: chip-reject
motion.purpose: Rejected time-chip edit feedback: a vermillion background fade instead of a silent revert. Pure color crossfade; safe under reduced motion.

breakpoints.name: stack-point
breakpoints.purpose: At and below this width, .main collapses from board+side-panel to a single column without shrinking the 720px recording artifact on ordinary laptop heights.

breakpoints.name: short-artifact
breakpoints.purpose: Only genuinely short desktop viewports opt into the 560px working-board fallback; ordinary 800-900px laptop heights keep the 720px artifact.

breakpoints.name: squeeze-920
breakpoints.purpose: Short-viewport tier: subtitle track 56px, tighter gaps and paddings.

breakpoints.name: squeeze-840
breakpoints.purpose: Shorter still: subtitle track 48px, 44px logo, and 8px console padding; this tier tightens chrome without changing artifact size.

breakpoints.name: mobile
breakpoints.purpose: Controls reflow to three rows; empty subtitle track collapses; board radius steps to 8px.

components.name: Primary Action Button (Play)
components.description: The single primary-action button in the chrome. The only gradient surface in the system. 44x44, brand-blue gradient, cream glyph, brand-bloom shadow, scale-on-hover.
components.html: <button class="ds-btn-primary" aria-label="Play"><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" width="22" height="22" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M7 5 L19 12 L7 19 Z" fill="currentColor"/></svg></button>
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { width: 44px; height: 44px; border: 0; border-radius: 10px; background: linear-gradient(135deg, #5d8fc9, #3a64a0); color: #f1ecde; display: grid; place-items: center; cursor: pointer; box-shadow: 0 6px 16px -6px rgba(93, 143, 201, 0.7); transition: transform 120ms ease-out; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { transform: scale(1.04); } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: scale(0.96); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #7da9dc; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Ghost Icon Button (Rewind)
components.description: Secondary transport action. 36x36, tonal-translucent surface, Rim-Light Pewter glyph. No gradient, no bloom, no scale on hover.
components.html: <button class="ds-btn-ghost" aria-label="Rewind to start"><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" width="18" height="18" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M5 5 v14 M19 5 L8 12 L19 19 Z" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linejoin="round"/></svg></button>
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { width: 36px; height: 36px; border: 0; border-radius: 10px; background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.06); color: #c8d0e6; display: grid; place-items: center; cursor: pointer; transition: background 150ms ease-out, color 150ms ease-out; } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.12); color: #e8ecf5; } .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #7da9dc; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Panel Mode Tabs (Script / Setup)
components.description: Full-width two-segment strip across the top of the side panel, sunk into a stagewell-black 24% recessed track. Tabs flex to half the panel width; the active state hooks on aria-selected, not a class.
components.css: .ds-tab-group { display: flex; gap: 4px; padding: 5px; background: rgba(15, 21, 37, 0.24); border-bottom: 1px solid rgba(232, 236, 245, 0.045); width: 100%; max-width: 420px; } .ds-tab { flex: 1 1 0; min-height: 40px; padding: 9px 12px; border: 0; border-radius: 7px; background: transparent; color: #aab3cf; font-family: 'Schibsted Grotesk', ui-sans-serif, sans-serif; font-weight: 700; font-size: 12.5px; cursor: pointer; transition: color 150ms ease-out, background 150ms ease-out; } .ds-tab:hover { color: #e8ecf5; } .ds-tab[aria-selected='true'] { background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.10); box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px rgba(232, 236, 245, 0.045); color: #e8ecf5; } .ds-tab:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #7da9dc; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Speed Selector
components.description: Four mono segments in a recessed stagewell-black 28% track. Reads like a video editor's transport-rate selector; the pressed treatment is shared with the Moves/Text view toggle.
components.css: .ds-speed-group { display: inline-flex; gap: 2px; padding: 3px; border-radius: 10px; background: rgba(15, 21, 37, 0.28); box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px rgba(232, 236, 245, 0.045); } .ds-speed-btn { border: 0; cursor: pointer; background: transparent; color: #8d97b3; padding: 5px 9px; border-radius: 5px; font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 11.5px; font-weight: 600; transition: color 150ms ease-out, background 150ms ease-out; } .ds-speed-btn:hover { color: #e8ecf5; } .ds-speed-btn[aria-pressed='true'] { background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.12); color: #e8ecf5; }

components.name: Side Panel
components.description: Container for the script editor and move list. 14px radius, chalk-wash surface (5.8% -> 2.8% vertical), 1px soft hairline, 8px load-bearing backdrop blur, 1px rim-light top inset.

Script

components.css: .ds-panel { width: 380px; height: 460px; display: flex; flex-direction: column; background: linear-gradient(180deg, rgba(232, 236, 245, 0.058), rgba(232, 236, 245, 0.028)); border: 1px solid rgba(232, 236, 245, 0.075); border-radius: 14px; overflow: hidden; backdrop-filter: blur(8px); box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 rgba(232, 236, 245, 0.06); } .ds-panel-header { padding: 16px 18px 13px; border-bottom: 1px solid rgba(232, 236, 245, 0.045); background: rgba(15, 21, 37, 0.11); } .ds-panel-title { margin: 0; font-family: 'Schibsted Grotesk', ui-sans-serif, sans-serif; font-size: 13px; font-weight: 700; text-transform: uppercase; color: #c8d0e6; } .ds-panel-hint { margin: 4px 0 0; font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 11.5px; color: #8d97b3; } .ds-panel-body { flex: 1; overflow-y: auto; padding: 8px 8px 16px; }

components.name: Pro-Grade Timeline Ruler
components.description: Signature component. Three-row sub-grid: kind-colored, kind-SHAPED marker pins above the rail (square-cut moves, capsule annotation pens, pointed pennants for structural breaks and script errors), the rail with brand-blue gradient fill, mono time ticks below, and a vertical playhead strand crossing all rows. Pins ride above the transparent scrub input so a pin click seeks its exact event; hover growth is a transform scale, never a height animation. One roving tab stop walks the pins with arrow keys.
components.html: 00:0000:1000:2000:30
components.css: .ds-timeline { position: relative; width: 100%; max-width: 480px; display: grid; grid-template-rows: 18px 6px 14px; row-gap: 5px; align-items: center; padding: 0 4px; } .ds-timeline-pins { position: relative; width: 100%; height: 100%; z-index: 5; pointer-events: none; } .ds-timeline-rail { position: relative; width: 100%; height: 6px; background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.08); border-radius: 999px; } .ds-scrub-fill { position: absolute; left: 0; top: 0; bottom: 0; background: linear-gradient(90deg, #5d8fc9, #7da9dc); border-radius: 999px; pointer-events: none; } .ds-timeline-ticks { position: relative; width: 100%; height: 14px; font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 10.5px; font-weight: 500; color: #8d97b3; } .ds-timeline-tick { position: absolute; top: 1px; transform: translateX(-50%); white-space: nowrap; } .ds-timeline-tick::before { content: ''; position: absolute; top: -7px; left: 50%; width: 1px; height: 4px; background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.10); transform: translateX(-50%); } .ds-playhead { position: absolute; top: -6px; bottom: 0; width: 1px; margin-left: -0.5px; background: linear-gradient(to bottom, rgba(232, 236, 245, 0.55) 0%, rgba(232, 236, 245, 0.55) 30%, rgba(232, 236, 245, 0.18) 100%); pointer-events: none; z-index: 3; } .ds-playhead-thumb { position: absolute; top: 24px; left: 50%; width: 14px; height: 14px; margin-left: -7px; margin-top: -7px; background: #e8ecf5; border-radius: 50%; box-shadow: 0 0 0 4px rgba(93, 143, 201, 0.35), 0 2px 6px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.4); } .ds-marker { position: absolute; top: 50%; transform: translate(-50%, -50%); width: 5px; height: 16px; border: 0; padding: 0; background: currentColor; border-radius: 2px; cursor: pointer; opacity: 0.85; transition: opacity 150ms ease-out, transform 150ms ease-out; pointer-events: auto; } .ds-marker::before { content: ''; position: absolute; inset: -22px -20px -6px; } .ds-marker:hover, .ds-marker:focus-visible { opacity: 1; transform: translate(-50%, -50%) scaleY(1.375); } .ds-marker::after { content: ''; position: absolute; left: 50%; top: 100%; width: 1px; height: 7px; margin-left: -0.5px; background: currentColor; opacity: 0.45; } .ds-marker-pen { border-radius: 999px; } .ds-marker-pennant { border-radius: 0; background: linear-gradient(to bottom right, transparent 48%, currentColor 52%) top left / 50% 30% no-repeat, linear-gradient(to bottom left, transparent 48%, currentColor 52%) top right / 50% 30% no-repeat, linear-gradient(currentColor, currentColor) bottom / 100% 70% no-repeat; }

components.name: Editable Time Chip
components.description: Click-to-edit timestamp pill attached to every timed event in the Moves view. 10.5px mono on a faint tonal pill so timestamps read as objects distinct from move numbers. A rejected (unparseable) edit flashes a vermillion color crossfade instead of reverting silently.
components.html: <button class="ds-time-chip" aria-label="Edit time of e4, currently 00:01.0">00:01</button> <button class="ds-time-chip ds-chip-rejected" aria-label="Edit time of Nf3">00:07.5</button>
components.css: .ds-time-chip { font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 10.5px; color: #8d97b3; border: 0; cursor: pointer; background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.06); padding: 1px 4px; border-radius: 999px; opacity: 0.9; transition: background 120ms ease-out, color 120ms ease-out; } .ds-time-chip:hover { background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.10); color: #e8ecf5; opacity: 1; } .ds-chip-rejected { animation: ds-chip-reject 650ms ease-out; } @keyframes ds-chip-reject { 0%, 35% { background: rgba(207, 93, 93, 0.4); color: #ffb4b4; box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px rgba(207, 93, 93, 0.7); } 100% { background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.06); } }

components.name: Move-List Seek Dot
components.description: Non-move events attach inline to the move they follow as kind-colored, kind-shaped dots: highlight squares off, arrow points, clear hollows to a ring. Dimmed until the playhead reaches them; the current one wears an outer ring.
components.html: e4
components.css: .ds-dot { width: 14px; height: 14px; padding: 0; border: 0; border-radius: 50%; background: transparent; cursor: pointer; position: relative; opacity: 0.95; display: inline-grid; place-items: center; vertical-align: middle; } .ds-dot-core { width: 7px; height: 7px; background: currentColor; border-radius: 50%; } .ds-dot-hl { border-radius: 1.5px; } .ds-dot-arrow { border-radius: 0; clip-path: polygon(12% 8%, 96% 50%, 12% 92%); } .ds-dot-clear { background: transparent; box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1.5px currentColor; }

narrative.overview: Gambit looks like a dim post-production room. The room is in deep navy blue lit by three radials: a steel-blue key light pooled on the board column, a warm wash from the upper-left, a cool wash from the lower-right. The chess board is the lit subject in the middle of the desk; everything around it (transport controls, the script panel, the move list) is the kind of quiet chrome a colorist or sound editor lives inside. The transport sitting under the board is a pro-grade timeline ruler with kind-colored, kind-shaped marker pins above the rail and mono time-tick labels below; between the board and the ruler sits the subtitle track, shown when SRT cues are loaded. The system rejects the chess.com palette outright, glassy AI-tool surfaces, candy-colored chess apps for kids, and the SaaS hero-metric template. There is exactly one accent gradient in the entire UI (the Play button); every other accent is a single solid color.
keyCharacteristics: Dark navy backdrop with a steel-blue key-light pool centered on the board column. Cream-on-blue board, never reversed.
Quiet tonal chrome. One gradient surface only (Play). One ambient drop shadow only (the board).
Typography is the structural device: monospaced for anything numeric or chess-script, sans for chrome titles.

Color marks meaning, not decoration. Move = blue, highlight = amber, arrow = persimmon, clear = grey-mist, reset/error = vermillion. These five hues drive every marker, scrub-fill, last-move tint, current-move pill, and current-event indicator — and each family also carries a shape, so kind is never color alone.
Pro-grade transport: marker pins above the rail, time-tick labels below, full-height playhead strand. The ruler is the signature component.
Motion is functional and exponential. Pieces slide via transform: translate3d, arrows draw, captures flash. Nothing hovers or shimmers.

rules.name: The Five Meanings Rule
rules.body: Five colors carry semantic load: blue for moves, amber for highlights, persimmon for arrows, grey-mist for clears, vermillion for resets and errors. Every timeline marker pin, every seek dot, the scrub-fill, the last-move tint, the current-move pill, and current non-move indicators pull from this list. Don't introduce a sixth without a sixth event kind to attach it to.

rules.name: The One Gradient Rule
rules.body: The system has exactly one accent gradient: the 44x44 Play button (linear-gradient(135deg, studio-steel-blue, deep-set-blue)). The scrubber's fill is a tonal blue gradient internal to the timeline component and counts as part of the same affordance, not a second gradient. Board-layer functional visuals (the capture flash, the check glow) are radial fades of a single palette color; they are part of the recorded artifact, not chrome accents. Every other accent is a single solid hex.

rules.name: The Annotation-Pens Rule
rules.body: Amber and Persimmon are not two colors; they are a pair, used together to imply a creator's two-pen toolkit. Highlights belong to Amber. Arrows belong to Persimmon. Don't cross them. Each pen is a two-stop family: a light board stop for overlay tints, a deeper marker stop for 5px chrome.

rules.name: The Mono-for-Chess Rule
rules.body: Anything chess-related (SAN, square coordinates, time codes, script lines) is set in JetBrains Mono. Anything chrome-related (the app title, panel titles, tab labels, button labels) is set in Schibsted Grotesk. The split is structural; do not mix.

rules.name: The Single-Display Rule
rules.body: The 23px Display weight appears once: the 'Gambit' wordmark. Subheadings, page titles, modal titles do not graduate to Display. If a future surface needs a larger label, use Headline at a larger size before promoting to Display.

rules.name: The Tonal-First Rule
rules.body: Surfaces stack via translucent whites, not shadows. If a new surface needs to read as elevated, raise its alpha by one stop on the 4/6/10/12 ladder before considering a real shadow.

rules.name: The One-Bloom Rule
rules.body: Brand bloom (the colored shadow) is reserved for the single primary action on any given surface. Never decorate two adjacent buttons with bloom; never put bloom on a non-action surface. The logo tile's bloom is the one header instance.

dos: Do keep chrome in the four-stop tonal ladder: rgba(255,255,255,α) at α ∈ {0.04, 0.06, 0.10, 0.12}. Anything outside this set should be a primitive accent color, not chrome.
Do set every numeric, every chess square, every SAN move, every script line in JetBrains Mono. Set every chrome label in Schibsted Grotesk.
Do use the move/highlight/arrow/clear/reset color list for any event-related visual. The five hues are vocabulary, not decoration.
Do keep functional motion (piece slide, arrow draw, capture flash) and cut everything else. Decorative hover pulses, gradient sweeps, shimmer effects: forbidden.
Do clamp all chrome contrast to quieter than the board. The board is the canvas. If chrome competes for attention in a screen recording, it is wrong.
donts: Don't use the chess.com palette. No green-and-cream board, no chess.com red-and-yellow accent set.
Don't ship the SaaS dashboard template. No hero-metric block, no identical icon-headline-blurb card grids, no gradient-accent CTAs scattered through the chrome.
Don't ship toy-chess vibes. No oversize rounded everything, no candy palette, no XP bars, badges, mascots, or gamified rewards. Cap component radius at 16px.

Don't ship the glassy AI-tool reflex. No stacked translucent panels, no neon glows, no gradient-mesh hero, no decorative backdrop-filter. The two existing blurs (controls 6px, side-col 8px) are load-bearing because they float over the board's color; that is the ceiling.

Don't introduce side-stripe borders as an accent device. Current event states use full-pill or full-row tinting plus dots and leading typographic contrast; they never grow a decorative side stripe. The textarea's :focus-visible strand is the one functional inset exception.
Don't use background-clip: text for gradient text anywhere. Single-color text, with hierarchy carried by weight and size.
Don't use modals as a first thought. The script editor lives in-panel, the move list lives in-panel; future affordances stay inline before they become modals.
Don't pure-#000 or pure-#fff anywhere. Stagewell Black (#0f1525) is the floor, Sodium Chalk (#e8ecf5) is the ceiling.

Don't animate CSS layout properties. Pieces translate via transform: translate3d(...) over a fixed origin, never via left/top. Animate transform, opacity, and box-shadow only. Easing curves are exponential ease-out; no bounce, no elastic, no spring.
